display_title: Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

head_commit.message:
Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

Nsight Systems (`nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu --profile-from-start off`) only record what runs between `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop`. JAX users currently call these through custom `ctypes` wrappers.

`jax.profiler.start_capture()`, `jax.profiler.stop_capture()`, and the `jax.profiler.capture()` context manager call new `start_capture` and `stop_capture` functions in the CUDA plugin extension. These call `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop` in the primary context of every device whose primary context is active, which are the contexts XLA runs its kernels in, so they work from any thread. The JAX functions raise `RuntimeError` on non-CUDA backends and with CUDA plugins that predate this change.

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Add benchmarks for closed-over constants and embedded_constants_max_bytes

Adds `constants_benchmark.py` and corresponding `constants_benchmark_cpu`,
`constants_benchmark_gpu`, and `constants_benchmark_tpu` targets to evaluate
trade-offs between embedding constants into lowered HLO vs hoisting them
as runtime executable arguments.

Focused on constant tensor sizes: 1KB, 4KB, 16KB, and 32KB.

Key Benchmark Findings (TPU & CPU):

1. TPU Benchmark Measurements (8 devices on Forge):
    Size     Exec Emb   Exec Hst   Exec Delta   Disp Emb   Disp Hst   Exe Emb    Exe Hst    Bloat
    1KB      68.44 us   67.40 us   -1.5%        34.30 us   33.61 us   49.7 KB    46.8 KB    1.1x
    4KB      66.08 us   66.05 us   -0.0%        33.04 us   36.18 us   59.0 KB    46.8 KB    1.3x
    16KB     67.10 us   69.63 us   +3.8%        35.53 us   34.30 us   95.9 KB    46.8 KB    2.0x
    32KB     66.57 us   66.65 us   +0.1%        32.43 us   33.72 us   142.7 KB   47.8 KB    3.1x

2. CPU Benchmark Measurements:
    Size     Exec Emb   Exec Hst   Exec Delta   Disp Emb   Disp Hst   Exe Emb    Exe Hst    Bloat
    1KB      15.43 us   15.64 us   +1.4%        12.37 us   12.96 us   7.3 KB     6.4 KB     1.1x
    4KB      25.21 us   24.41 us   -3.2%        17.71 us   18.88 us   9.7 KB     5.7 KB     1.7x
    16KB     29.47 us   29.44 us   -0.1%        16.82 us   16.96 us   22.0 KB    5.7 KB     3.8x
    32KB     34.21 us   35.72 us   +4.4%        16.81 us   17.86 us   38.4 KB    5.7 KB     6.7x

3. Analysis of Executable Bloat on TPU:
- Execution latency on TPU remains flat (~66-68 us) regardless of whether constants
  are embedded or hoisted.
- However, executable binary size grows rapidly when embedding constants:
  from 1.1x at 1KB (+2.9 KB) to 2.0x at 16KB (+49.1 KB) and 3.1x at 32KB (+94.9 KB).
- The current default threshold of 1024 bytes (jax_embedded_constants_max_bytes=1024)
  is well-calibrated: it eliminates argument passing overhead for small scalar
  and shape constants while avoiding the executable code bloat of larger thresholds.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Use backtracking search for whole-axis assignment in _create_device_mesh_for_nd_torus.

head_commit.message:
Use backtracking search for whole-axis assignment in _create_device_mesh_for_nd_torus.

The greedy first-fit assignment commits to its most-preferred candidate
for each logical axis without reconsidering, which can strand the
remaining logical axes even though a whole-axis mapping exists. On a TPU
v7/v7x topology of (x, y, z, core) = (4, 4, 8, 2), the core-axis priority
assigns the logical axis of size 16 to (z, core), after which the logical
axes of size 8 and 2 cannot be mapped, so create_device_mesh((2, 8, 16))
raises NotImplementedError despite 2 -> core, 8 -> z, 16 -> x*y being
available. All legal 256-device v7 topologies fail this way, since a
logical axis of size 2 can only map to the core axis.

Search the candidates in their preference order with backtracking (with
memoized failed states) instead of committing to the first fit. This
returns the same assignment as first-fit whenever first-fit succeeds, so
existing meshes are unaffected, and falls back to splitting physical axes
only when no whole-axis mapping exists at all, as documented.

Fixes #42879.

Signed-off-by: wangfakang <fakangwang@gmail.com>

display_title: Fix lax.polynomial derivatives when x broadcasts against coefficients.

head_commit.message:
Fix lax.polynomial derivatives when x broadcasts against coefficients.

When differentiating `lax.polynomial(x, coeffs)` with respect to `x`, the constant coefficient `coeffs[0]` is dropped when computing the derivative polynomial. If `coeffs[0]` had a larger shape than `x` and the remaining coefficients, the resulting tangent was not broadcast to the output shape. Combine tangent terms with `lax.add` and broadcast the output tangent to match the primal output shape and sharding.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42480

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029826485

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Support TF32 MMAs with K-fastest operands on Blackwell.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support TF32 MMAs with K-fastest operands on Blackwell.

`tcgen05.mma` accepted float32 operands, but could not issue them: the
instruction descriptor had no encoding for TF32, and `.kind::tf32` was missing.
It now issues `tcgen05.mma.kind::tf32` for float32 A (in SMEM or TMEM) and B,
with float32 accumulators.

The MMA truncates the float32 mantissas of its operands to the 10 bits of TF32
rather than rounding them, unlike XLA's TF32 matmuls, which round to nearest
even. Callers that want XLA's results must round the operands first, e.g. with
`jax.lax.reduce_precision`.

M- or N-fastest TF32 operands need the 128B swizzle with 32B atoms, which Mosaic
GPU does not support. With the other swizzles, the MMA leaves the accumulator
unchanged (zeros in the tests), so `tcgen05.mma` raises `NotImplementedError`
for them instead.

display_title: Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

head_commit.message:
Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

Nsight Systems (`nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu --profile-from-start off`) only record what runs between `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop`. JAX users currently call these through custom `ctypes` wrappers.

`jax.profiler.start_capture()`, `jax.profiler.stop_capture()`, and the `jax.profiler.capture()` context manager call new `start_capture` and `stop_capture` functions in the CUDA plugin extension. These call `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop` in the primary context of every device whose primary context is active, which are the contexts XLA runs its kernels in, so they work from any thread. The JAX functions raise `RuntimeError` on non-CUDA backends and with CUDA plugins that predate this change.

display_title: Improve error reporting when a traced value is passed for a reduction axis

head_commit.message:
Improve error reporting when a traced value is passed for a reduction axis

Passing a vmapped array as the `axis` argument of a reduction, like doing `vmap(lambda x, y: jnp.sum(x, y))(x, ys)` previously raised a ConcretizationTypeError that only said:

"The axis argument must be known statically."

It doesn't specify which function the axis is being passed to or why the value isn't static even w/ vmap.

Now `name` gets passed to `_ensure_optional_axes` every time the function is called, so the message actually names the function, like: "The axis argument to jnp.sum() must be known statically."

`BatchTracer._origin_msg` also explains that vmapped values takes different values for each batch element, thus not having any single concrete value. This is like how `jit` tracers explain which argument they depend on. For unmapped tracers, of course, we skip the explanation.(`batch_dim is None`).

Also extended test `test_invalid_shape_error_with_jit_tracer_passed` and added test `testTracedAxisErrorNamesFunction` to check for the vmap explanation and the function name, respectively.

Fixes #10493

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Fix jnp.quantile output shape for 0-d inputs with keepdims=True

head_commit.message:
Fix jnp.quantile output shape for 0-d inputs with keepdims=True

With axis=None, `_quantile` stores the kept-dims shape as `[1] * a.ndim`
and ravels the input. For a 0-d input that shape is `[]`, which the
later `if keepdims and keepdim:` checks treat as unset, so the raveled
`(1,)` result was returned instead of `()` (or `(len(q), 1)` instead of
`(len(q),)` for vector `q`). Use `None` as the unset value. This affects
`jnp.quantile`, `jnp.percentile`, `jnp.median`, and their nan variants.

head_commit.message:
Disable kCFI checks on client-side PJRT C API and plugin profiler calls.

When a client built with Universal CFI (-fsanitize=kcfi) invokes function
pointers provided by a separately built or prebuilt PJRT/profiler plugin
without kCFI type hashes (such as prebuilt libtpu.so), indirect calls across
the C ABI boundary trap with SIGILL.

Wrap the raw C function-pointer invocations in a file-local
ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI `NoCfiCall` helper so CFI checks are skipped
only for the cross-plugin indirect calls while preserving CFI checks on all
surrounding C++ calls. Covers the five files exercised by failing tests:
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_helpers.cc
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_status_utils.cc
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_abi_version_helpers.cc

display_title: Disable kCFI checks on client-side PJRT C API and plugin profiler calls.

head_commit.message:
Disable kCFI checks on client-side PJRT C API and plugin profiler calls.

When a client built with Universal CFI (-fsanitize=kcfi) invokes function
pointers provided by a separately built or prebuilt PJRT/profiler plugin
without kCFI type hashes (such as prebuilt libtpu.so), indirect calls across
the C ABI boundary trap with SIGILL.

Wrap the raw C function-pointer invocations in a file-local
ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_CFI `NoCfiCall` helper so CFI checks are skipped
only for the cross-plugin indirect calls while preserving CFI checks on all
surrounding C++ calls. Covers the five files exercised by failing tests:
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_helpers.cc
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_status_utils.cc
- xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_abi_version_helpers.cc
- xla/backends/profiler/plugin/plugin_tracer.cc
- jaxlib/xla.cc

head_commit.message:
Disable XLA GPU autotuning in nn_test.

Profiling nn_test on B200 showed that over 90% of wall time is spent in XLA GPU compilation, with roughly half of total runtime going to GPU GEMM/einsum autotuning on small test tensors (for example, Triton GEMM autotuning in attention and scaled-matmul tests).

Set `XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0"` on `nn_test`, cutting total B200 test runtime across all 10 shards nearly in half (from 670s to 361s, with max shard time dropping from 84s to 44s).

display_title: Use C++20 `std::make_unique_for_overwrite` in jaxlib.

head_commit.message:
Use C++20 `std::make_unique_for_overwrite` in jaxlib.

Replaces `absl::make_unique_for_overwrite`, zero-initializing `std::make_unique<T[]>` calls for immediately overwritten scratch buffers, raw `new[]`/`delete[]` buffer management, and the custom `HostBuffer` allocator with `std::make_unique_for_overwrite<T[]>`.

In `py_client_gpu.cc`, manages temporary input, transpose, and packed return buffers with `std::unique_ptr<char[]>`, fixing leaks on early return and keeping packed return buffers alive through `gpuStreamSynchronize`. In `lapack_kernels.cc`, moves the `ABSL_ANNOTATE_MEMORY_IS_INITIALIZED` annotation for `ipiv_tmp` before the loop that reads it.

head_commit.message:
Use C++20 defaulted `operator==` and remove redundant `operator!=` in jaxlib.

Replace hand-written memberwise `operator==` definitions with `= default` on
`BitMask::Iterator`, `ReentrantHashSet::iterator`,
`ReentrantHashSet::const_iterator`, `TracebackEntry`, `ColorState`,
`PyArgSignature`, `ShapedArrayCacheKey`, and `GroupKey`, and remove redundant
`operator!=` overloads (including on `ArgumentSignature`, `CallSignature`, and
`PyTreeDef`, which keep their custom `operator==`).

Reorder `PyArgSignature::weak_type` before `shape` so defaulted comparison
preserves cheap-first evaluation order and eliminates 8 bytes of padding; drop
the now-unused `<tuple>` include.

display_title: Use C++20 `<bit>` utilities in jaxlib.

head_commit.message:
Use C++20 `<bit>` utilities in jaxlib.

Replace compiler builtins, `absl` bit utilities, and manual bit-twiddling with
standard C++20 `<bit>` equivalents, and guard little-endian assumptions with
`static_assert`:

- `reentrant_hash_set.h`: replace `__builtin_ctz` with `std::countr_zero`.
- `mosaic/gpu/dump.cc`: replace `absl::has_single_bit` and `absl::countr_zero`
  with `std::has_single_bit` and `std::countr_zero`, and drop the
  `absl/numeric:bits` dependency.
- `mosaic/gpu/runtime.cc`: replace the manual power-of-two assertion with
  `std::has_single_bit`.
- `gpu/sparse_kernels.cc`: add a `static_assert` on `std::endian::native`
  being little-endian in `ConstOne`.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

head_commit.message:
Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

Nsight Systems (`nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu --profile-from-start off`) only record what runs between `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop`. JAX users currently call these through custom `ctypes` wrappers.

`jax.profiler.start_capture()`, `jax.profiler.stop_capture()`, and the `jax.profiler.capture()` context manager call new `start_capture` and `stop_capture` functions in the CUDA plugin extension. These call `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop` in the primary context of every device whose primary context is active, which are the contexts XLA runs its kernels in, so they work from any thread. The JAX functions raise `RuntimeError` on non-CUDA backends and with CUDA plugins that predate this change.
